title: Λέων καὶ ὄνος ⟨ὁμοῦ θηρεύοντες⟩
titleEn: The Lion and the Donkey Hunting Together
part: The Lion and the Donkey Hunting Together (Chambry 208 · Perry 151)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 208 (= Perry 151). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« », ⟨ ⟩ for editorial supplements). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Λέων καὶ ὄνος κοινωνίαν πρὸς ἀλλήλους ποιησάμενοι ἐξῆλθον ἐπὶ θήραν.
sentences.tr: Leōn kai onos koinōnian pros allēlous poiēsamenoi exēlthon epi thēran.
sentences.l: A lion and a donkey, having made a partnership with each other, went out to the hunt.
sentences.n: ποιησάμενοι is middle: they made the arrangement for themselves, as parties to it. Chambry's title carries ⟨ὁμοῦ θηρεύοντες⟩, 'hunting together', in angle brackets — his own supplement, not part of the transmitted title.

sentences.t: Γενομένων δὲ αὐτῶν κατά τι σπήλαιον ἐν ᾧ ἦσαν αἶγες ἄγριαι, ὁ μὲν λέων πρὸ τοῦ στομίου στὰς ἐξιούσας παρετηρεῖτο, ὁ δὲ εἰσελθὼν ἐνήλατό τε αὐταῖς καὶ ὠγκᾶτο ἐκφοβεῖν βουλόμενος.
sentences.tr: Genomenōn de autōn kata ti spēlaion en hōi ēsan aiges agriai, ho men leōn pro tou stomiou stas exiousas paretēreito, ho de eiselthōn enēlato te autais kai ōnkato ekphobein boulomenos.
sentences.l: And they having come to a certain cave in which there were wild goats, the lion, standing before the mouth of it, watched for them as they came out, while the other, having gone in, leapt among them and brayed, wishing to frighten them out.
sentences.i: When they had come to a cave with wild goats in it, the lion took his stand before the mouth and watched for them as they came out, while the donkey went inside, sprang in among them and brayed, meaning to frighten them out.
sentences.n: μέν and δέ divide the labour, and the division is the joke: the lion does the killing, the donkey does the noise. στόμιον is the mouth of the cave, the narrow place where everything must pass. παρετηρεῖτο is imperfect middle, the sustained watching of an ambush.

sentences.t: Τοῦ δὲ λέοντος τὰς πλείστας συλλαβόντος, ἐξελθὼν ἐπυνθάνετο αὐτοῦ εἰ γενναίως ἠγωνίσατο καὶ τὰς αἶγας ἐξεδίωξεν.
sentences.tr: Tou de leontos tas pleistas syllabontos, exelthōn epynthaneto autou ei gennaiōs ēgōnisato kai tas aigas exediōxen.
sentences.l: And the lion having caught most of them, he came out and asked him whether he had fought nobly and driven the goats out.
sentences.i: When the lion had caught most of them, the donkey came out and asked the lion whether he himself had fought nobly and driven the goats out.
sentences.n: πυνθάνομαι takes the genitive of the person questioned. εἰ introduces the indirect question and the tenses of the direct question stand unchanged — 'did I fight nobly?' becomes 'whether he fought nobly'. ἀγωνίζομαι belongs to the games and the battlefield, which is exactly the standing the donkey is claiming.

sentences.t: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· « Ἀλλ’ εὖ ἴσθι ὅτι κἀγὼ ἄν σε ἐφοβήθην, εἰ μὴ ᾔδειν σε ὄνον ὄντα. »
sentences.tr: Ho de eipen· « All’ eu isthi hoti kagō an se ephobēthēn, ei mē ēidein se onon onta. »
sentences.l: And he said: « Well, know it well that I too would have been afraid of you, if I had not known that you were a donkey. »
sentences.n: A past contrary-to-fact condition: ἄν with the aorist indicative in the main clause, εἰ with the past ᾔδειν in the protasis — it did not happen, and the reason it did not is stated. ᾔδειν takes the supplementary participle ὄντα for what was known. κἀγώ is a crasis of καὶ ἐγώ.

sentences.t: Οὕτως οἱ παρὰ τοῖς εἰδόσιν ἀλαζονευόμενοι εἰκότως γέλωτα ὀφλισκάνουσιν.
sentences.tr: Houtōs hoi para tois eidosin alazoneuomenoi eikotōs gelōta ophliskanousin.
sentences.l: Thus those who play the braggart among those who know incur ridicule, and with good reason.
sentences.n: γέλωτα ὀφλισκάνειν borrows from the courts: ὀφλισκάνω is to lose one's case and so be sentenced to pay, and what is exacted here is laughter. ὁ ἀλαζών is the impostor who claims what is not his.
